topic: How are link budgets affected when prioritizing high-revenue services versus navigation safety margins in dynamic scheduling?
consensus_response: Dynamic scheduling prioritizes revenue-generating services, leading to increased interference on shared links. This directly impacts available bandwidth for mission-critical operations like navigation, impacting QoS guarantees even with advanced modulation schemes. Advanced techniques like AMC and adaptive modulation schemes can mitigate this impact but don't guarantee QoS guarantees if the network is overloaded.  The inherent tradeoff necessitates careful planning to balance competing demands.
reference_context: Satellite networks face a challenge balancing high-revenue services (e.g., streaming) with safety margins (e.g., navigation). Dynamic scheduling, prioritizing revenue services over safety, creates congestion, hindering QoS guarantees even with advanced modulation schemes.  Link budgets are limited by antenna noise and signal strength, requiring careful planning to optimize resource allocation.
